experiment: PX-4 (rtx-11): streaming/restructured FlashAttention for the 128k full-layer prefill tail
gpu: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, 97887 MiB, single GPU (sm_120a / cc 12.0, 188 SMs, L2 128 MiB, 1792 GB/s HBM)
scope: ONLY the 8 FULL hd512 causal layers (nh16 / nkv1, hd512, O(ctx^2)); the 40 sliding hd256 layers are window-capped and untouched (byte-identical).
change: d_flash_prefill_px4<512,32,16> (op_attention.cuh, PLOW_NV_FA_PX4=1 default, hd512 arm only): (a) REGISTER softmax fused into the P.V mma A-fragment — each P.V warp computes P for its own 16 query rows in the mma m16n8k16 A layout via quad-shfl row reductions, m/l/corr live in registers, so the Ps smem buffer, its ldmatrix, and one __syncthreads are removed; (b) 8-warp QK — the HD-512 contraction splits into two hd halves (SsA hd0..255 / SsB hd256..511) summed at the softmax read, halving the dependent-mma-chain depth and putting the 4 QK-idle warps of the T5 grid to work; (c) optional TMA (cp.async.bulk + mbarrier per-row KV staging, PLOW_NV_FA_TMA=1) A/B'd vs cp.async.cg. hd256 sliding arm keeps the T5 path byte-identical.
baseline_note: The rtx-11-px4-roofline.md 'measured mma 21.9/147.2/1019.4 ms' is the PIPE=0 (T4 synchronous-staging) path, NOT the shipping default. The shipping default is PIPE=1 (T5 cp.async KV-stream), measured here at 11.85/78.61/345.6 ms — already ~3x faster than the roofline baseline at 128k. Both are reported below; PX-4's honest A/B is vs T5 (the real ship point).
profiling_note: ncu (dram__throughput etc.) is UNAVAILABLE in this container (ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM, RmProfilingAdminOnly=1). Achieved DRAM BW is derived analytically: bytes = FA-re-read floor 68.99 GB (= roofline 38.5 ms x 1792 GB/s at 128k) / measured time. A phase ablation harness (runtime/nvidia/experiments/px4_fa_ablate.cu) substitutes for ncu counters for the compute/latency attribution.

correctness_gate.oracle: sm120_interp_op_test full flash-prefill suite PASS in BOTH staging arms (cp.async and TMA) vs the T4-FIXED f32 CPU reference (masked->0, the sensitive oracle): 26 flash_pre cases (causal / sliding-window straddle / hd256+512 / fused ns=1 / split ns>1 + merge / ragged / chunked seq_q<seq_kv q_pos0>0 / soft-softmax) relL2 1.5e-3..2.4e-3, same bf16-P precision band as T5; whole suite ok; wave64 negctrl still FAILs.
correctness_gate.token_identity: gemma-4-12B, PLOW_PREFILL=1 vs PLOW_PREFILL=0 (decode-only reference). First-gen token AGREES at ctx 256/4k/32k/128k (all = 236770). PX4 prefill step-0 top-5 logits are BIT-IDENTICAL to the T5 baseline prefill (19.00000/18.25000/15.56250/14.81250/14.75000). device==host argmax AGREE.

microbench.harness: runtime/nvidia/experiments/fa_pv_bench.cu, d_flash_prefill<512,32,16>, grid 188 / 256 threads, nsplit=1, seq_q=8192 tail chunk, q_pos0=seq_kv-seq_q, zeroed data, cudaEvent, warmup 2.

achieved_dram_bw_128k.method: derived (ncu unavailable): 68.99 GB / time; floor = 38.5 ms (FA re-read, KV>L2) / 1792 GB/s peak / compute floor 139.7 ms (per rtx-11-px4-roofline.md).

ablation_128k.harness: runtime/nvidia/experiments/px4_fa_ablate.cu (byte-faithful T5-shape kernel, per-phase compile-time null with all barriers/commits/waits kept). Substitutes for ncu.
ablation_128k.reading: cp.async-issue-skip removes only 16%, per-tile time is FLAT 8k->128k => the hd512 flash is NOT DRAM-bandwidth-bound (it is compute/latency-bound: softmax + QK dominate). This is why PX-4 attacked the compute geometry (register softmax + 8-warp QK), not just streaming, and why TMA (a pure streaming lever) is a NEGATIVE.

e2e_prefill.harness: gemma4_sm120_chat, gemma-4-12B, PLOW_PREFILL=1, batch1, TP1, greedy, pkt gemma4-12b-ctx132096-b1. prefill_ms = pure prefill wall (KV build, excl. first decode). PX4 vs a same-session PLOW_NV_FA_PX4=0 (T5) control binary.
e2e_prefill.reading: The e2e win grows with ctx (as the 8 full-layer O(ctx^2) flash share rises): -1.4%@4k -> -15.7%@128k, saving 5.85 s of a 37.4 s prefill at 128k. Only the 8 full layers changed; the 40 sliding layers and all GEMM are untouched, so the flash-op-level -24% dilutes to -15.7% e2e at 128k. Baseline 37363 ms reproduces the committed T5 e2e (37223 ms @131000).

ptxas.px4_cpasync: k_fa_pre<512,32,16> 96 regs / 0 spill (was ~210 in T5 — register softmax + no Ps buffer); prefill _pf megakernel 240 regs / 0 spill / occ-1; dynamic smem union unchanged at 79.75 KiB (hd256 sliding arm dominates; PX4 hd512 arena SHRINKS to 69.0 KiB).

negatives: TMA (cp.async.bulk + mbarrier) KV staging is ~2x SLOWER than cp.async.cg at every ctx (20.7/138.7/610.6 vs 9.08/59.68/261.96 ms). Root cause: sm_120 single-CTA TMA issues one bulk copy per contiguous row from ONE thread (no .tensor 2D tiling that would batch the 16 BKV rows), serializing 16 per-row descriptors while cp.async.cg spreads 16B lines across all 256 threads. Consistent with rtx-05/gemv_transport 'TMA refuted for small/1-D streams'. Kept behind PLOW_NV_FA_TMA=0 (opt-in) as a measured negative.

The roofline framed PX-4 partly as a KV-streaming/bandwidth problem. The ablation DISPROVES that for the hd512 flash: it is compute/latency-bound (cp.async-issue removal saves only 16%), so a pure streaming lever (TMA) cannot help — the win came from the compute-geometry restructure (register softmax + 8-warp QK).
